stories.label: Trump raises doubts about renewed attacks on Iran
stories.summary: New since the two-day Hormuz offer covered at 18:00 and Axios's report that Netanyahu pressed for strikes after the midterms: Trump, asked directly, played down renewed strikes on Iran after Tuesday's vote, citing diplomatic progress, and The New Arab reports a Qatari delegation heading to Tehran to continue mediation. Lead with his words and what binds him to them: nothing has been signed, and the Doha talks ended without a deal. Those who live with the gap are Iranians, and crews and residents in the Gulf. Write from Reuters and Al Jazeera; TRT World and TASS are state media and are attributed if used. The Middle East Eye link is a liveblog entry. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The oil market's response runs as a separate entry. Dateline Tehran, unless the source places the remarks in the US, in which case it still does not count against the cap as US policy felt elsewhere.

stories.label: Shooting heard near house near Kiev where mobilized are forcibly held
stories.summary: Hundreds protested at a private house in Petropavlovskaya Borshchagovka outside Kyiv where mobilized men and deserters were reportedly held in the basement; TASS, citing the Ukrainian outlet Strana, reports gunfire by law enforcement and four escapees injured. Lead with the men in the basement. The surprising line is from the head of Zelensky's office, as TASS reports it: only 14 people were held rather than 40, and many such buildings exist across Ukraine (https://tass.com/world/2212125; on the Azov link, https://tass.com/world/2212127). The mechanism is what a war's manpower shortage does to the men it conscripts. TASS is Russian state media and a party to this war, and is the only source in the feed: say 'Russian state news agency TASS reported', state nothing as fact on its word, seek Strana or Ukrainian confirmation, and give Kyiv's account. Dateline Petropavlivska Borshchahivka.

stories.label: Zelensky warns Russia could exploit US midterms to launch massive attack
stories.summary: Zelensky says Ukrainian intelligence shows Russia preparing a massive attack on energy and logistics, timed to Tuesday's US midterm vote. Lead with the target and who pays: civilians going into winter without power, and the humanitarian supply lines the source describes around Zaporizhzhia, including at Komyshuvakha, as far as it says. It is one side's intelligence claim and no attack has happened, so attribute it and say what evidence he offers and what Moscow answers. Dateline Kyiv, or Zaporizhzhia if the source leads there; not a US story, so it does not count against the cap.

stories.label: Mike Rogers Earned $420,000 From Firm Now Helping Hegseth Plan Iran War‘s Next Phase
stories.summary: New since the Israel foreign-agent filings covered 1 November, and a separate matter: after leaving Congress, Michigan Senate candidate Mike Rogers took $420,000 in board fees from MITRE, the consultancy Pete Hegseth has tapped to help plan the future of warfare. Lead with the sum and the contract, on the eve of the vote. The accountability question: a man seeking a seat that oversees the Pentagon, paid by a firm working for it. Say over which years he was paid, what MITRE is contracted to do, whether Rogers still holds any tie, and his answer. Do not imply wrongdoing the documents do not show. Not the horse race. US pick 1 of 3. Dateline Detroit, or Washington if the source places it there.

stories.label: Judge dismisses charges against FBI agents involved in Hunter Biden case
stories.summary: New since the charges covered 23 October: a US magistrate judge dismissed the criminal case against two former senior FBI officials accused of lying to Congress about Hunter Biden, after their lawyers attacked a hurried and inaccurate prosecution. Lead with the judge's grounds, in the judge's words. The stake: whether a Justice Department under Trump can charge officials over his old grievances, and what a court now says about how it did so, on the eve of the midterms. Say whether the dismissal bars refiling and what the department answers. US pick 2 of 3. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: Interactive: Who wants what at the COP31 climate change summit
stories.summary: Carbon Brief has mapped what each bloc is demanding as delegates head for COP31 in Antalya, under the shadow of war. Lead with the sharpest gap in its tracker, between those who pay and those who are exposed, in the figures it gives. Name the blocs and positions, and where the Muslim-majority and small-island states stand, as far as the source says. China's goals and the Pacific pre-COP ran in October, so do not repeat them. These are negotiating positions, not outcomes. Filed under politics because it is a negotiation, not a finding. Dateline Antalya.

stories.label: Brent crude price falls below $104 per barrel, first time since October 15
stories.summary: New since this morning's report of a 3% fall: Brent crude was down 8.55% at $103.73 by the evening, below $104 for the first time since 15 October, while Iran offers a two-day Hormuz reopening and Trump plays down strikes. Lead with the size of a one-day fall on words alone: no ship has been promised safe passage, and the attacks in the strait go on. Say who gains from cheaper oil, and who is still paying, among Asian importers and crews, as far as the sources go. The price is TASS's report, Russian state media and the only source in the feed: attribute it and check it against the live Brent series. Name Brent crude, WTI and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Filed under economy; the Iran diplomacy runs as a separate entry. Dateline London, where the contract trades.

stories.label: Less than 10% of Nigerian property have proper land titles - Finance Ministry
stories.summary: Fewer than 10% of properties in Nigeria have proper titles, says Armstrong Takang, managing director of the Ministry of Finance Incorporated (MOFI). Lead with that number and its mechanism: people own assets they cannot borrow against, so homes cannot serve as collateral. Say who holds the power to grant title, what it costs and how long it takes, as far as the source does, and what MOFI proposes and stands to gain. It is an official's figure, so attribute it and say what it rests on. Do not imply a reform has begun if only a plan exists. Filed under economy; the feed's politics tag is wrong. Dateline Abuja unless the source places it elsewhere.

stories.label: 长安汽车三季报：海外销量大涨，利润却快没了
stories.summary: Changan Automobile's third-quarter report shows overseas sales surging while profit has nearly vanished, TMTPost reports from mainland China. Lead with those two figures side by side. The mechanism: what China's price war at home and the cost of going abroad do to a state-owned carmaker's margin, as far as the source says, and which markets take the cars. It tests the export story told about Chinese carmakers. Keep TMTPost's judgments attributed and take figures from the filing as it reports them. Source is Chinese; the writer reads it. Filed under economy; the feed's tech tag is wrong. Dateline Chongqing.

stories.label: Cheap version of HIV-prevention shot raising hope in low-income countries
stories.summary: The US FDA approved a generic version of the world's only twice-a-year shot to prevent HIV, opening the way to a cheap supply for low-income countries. Lead with the price: the brand's against the generic's, and how many people in which countries it could reach, as far as the source says. The mechanism: who holds the licence, Gilead's terms, Unitaid's role, and which countries a licence leaves out, if the source names them. An approval is not a delivery, so say when doses arrive and who pays. Filed under science as trial-backed medicine; the feed's politics tag is wrong. FDA action felt elsewhere does not count against the US cap. Dateline where the source places the lead maker or rollout; Johannesburg if it gives Africa and no city.

stories.label: Washington state resident dies from bird flu following exposure to infected cattle
stories.summary: A Yakima County resident with prior health conditions has died of bird flu after exposure at an infected dairy, the third US death since the virus began jumping to livestock and the first in a year. Lead with the route of infection and what is known of the strain. The mechanism: a virus still quietly spreading through dairy herds, and how much testing of cattle and of farm workers there actually is, as far as the sources say; Ars Technica has a second report (https://arstechnica.com/health/2026/11/third-person-dies-of-bird-flu-since-virus-started-jumping-to-livestock/). Officials still call the public risk low, so report that and whether there is any evidence of human-to-human spread. US pick 3 of 3. Dateline Yakima.

stories.label: Most of our measures of a key cognitive process don't agree
stories.summary: A big study found that most of the ways researchers measure a key cognitive process do not agree with one another, and it reached print despite being nearly all negative results. Lead with which process, how many measures and how many people, and how weak the agreement was. The stake: years of findings, and treatments such as cognitive therapy that lean on these measures, may be measuring different things, only as far as the study supports that. Name the journal and the authors. Filed under science; the feed's politics tag is wrong. Dateline where the lead institution is; if it is in the US it does not fit the cap, so use the institution's non-US co-lead if the study has one, otherwise omit the place.

stories.label: KI, Cloud und Open Source: Die EU sucht die digitale Souveränität
stories.summary: The European Commission's digital sovereignty push has chosen industrial AI applications over building its own frontier models, and its sovereign-cloud plans leave a door open for US companies, netzpolitik.org reports. Lead with that door: what the rules let a US cloud provider do and still count as sovereign. The stake is who could cut Europe off, and who keeps its data, as far as the source says. Say what is proposed and what is decided, and what the open-source part would actually bind. Keep netzpolitik's verdicts attributed. Source is German; the writer reads it. Dateline Brussels.

stories.label: Lebanon’s Fight for Digital Sovereignty, Reimagined
stories.summary: Through three years of war, people in Lebanon turned to WhatsApp rather than television for news of what was happening, which puts a country's wartime information in the hands of one foreign company. Lead with that dependency and one concrete consequence the source gives: a takedown, a blocked account, or a shutdown. The mechanism: who can moderate or cut that channel, and what SMEX says Lebanon could build or demand instead. SMEX is a digital-rights advocate, so attribute its proposals as its own and report what has actually been done. Dateline Beirut.

stories.label: The Brazilian left’s quest to ‘tame’ Meta: A narrative of denouncement and resistance
stories.summary: A Brazilian movement, the 'Não se Meta' campaign, is organizing online against Meta's content moderation and governance. Lead with what the campaign accuses Meta of, with one case, and what it asks for. The mechanism: how a US company's moderation rules reach Brazilian politics, and what Brazil's courts and government can do about it, as far as the source says. Report Meta's answer if the source has one, and say that Global Voices is analysing a narrative rather than reporting a ruling. Filed under tech; the feed's politics tag is secondary. Picked in part because the audit found no Latin America dateline. Dateline São Paulo, or Brasília if the source leads there.

stories.label: Iran says in 'intensive' negotiations with US to avert war
stories.summary: New since the Doha talks ended without a deal: Iran's foreign ministry says it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz in two days, down from its earlier one-week timeline, if the US meets its conditions, and that 'intensive' contacts continue. Lead with the shortened timeline and the conditions attached, on the eve of the 3 November date both sides have named. Say what Washington has answered and who is held hostage to the gap: crews in the strait and Gulf importers. It is an offer and not a reopening. The Times of Israel link is a liveblog entry, so write from the New York Times, Hindustan Times, Straits Times and news24 reports in the sources. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: Israeli opposition rallies behind Eisenkot as Herzog opens consultations on next government
stories.summary: New since the election race covered in October: opposition parties will recommend that President Herzog task Gadi Eisenkot with forming a government, and expected recommendations from Arab parties could raise him to 67 lawmakers. Lead with that arithmetic and its catch: Arab votes may carry him to the mandate, while their role in any government stays unclear, as Al-Monitor reports. What would it change for Palestinians, in Gaza and inside Israel, as far as the sources say? Do not imply a coalition exists. Write from Al Jazeera and Al-Monitor; TRT World is state media and is attributed if used. Dateline Jerusalem, not the feed's Gaza tag.

stories.label: Attacks on ships in Strait of Hormuz 'could be higher than official count' | The National
stories.summary: The head of the UN's International Maritime Organization said on Monday that attacks on ships crossing the Strait of Hormuz outnumber the official figures, because shadow-fleet owners tend not to report them. Lead with the official count and that warning: the tally everyone cites, markets included, leaves out the least protected crews. The mechanism: false flags, switched-off AIS and owners with reasons to stay silent, as far as the source says. Say what becomes of those crews and whether the IMO offers an estimate; if it gives none, say so. Not the two-day reopening offer, which runs separately. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Dateline London if the IMO head spoke there, otherwise where the source places it.

stories.label: Israeli strikes kill 13 Palestinians in Gaza; UN staffer dies in Ansarallah detention; Haley Stevens’ meltdown
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed 13 Palestinians in Gaza, Drop Site reports in its daily roundup. Lead with those killed: where, how, and their names and ages if the source has them, with the toll attributed to whoever gave it. Say what the strikes were aimed at according to the Israeli military, if it answered. Use the Gaza item only, with a clause at most on the UN staffer who died in Ansarallah detention in Yemen, and leave out the Michigan item, already covered. Dateline Gaza City, or where the source places the strikes.

stories.label: Timeline of US Strikes Against Alleged Drug Boats
stories.summary: New since the toll of 243 covered on 28 October: the US military launched five strikes on alleged drug boats in as many days last week, one of the deadliest weeks of a campaign running since September, InSight Crime reports. Lead with those five strikes and their dead. The accountability point: people killed at sea without charge or trial, on an allegation no court tests, and few of them named. Give the running toll as the source does, say what evidence has been published about any boat, and keep 'drug boats' as Washington's allegation. US policy felt elsewhere, so it does not count against the US cap. Dateline where the source places the latest strike, Caribbean or eastern Pacific, or Bogotá if it gives no place.

stories.label: The world has a new plan to save nature, but it still needs the money
stories.summary: Leaders at the UN biodiversity summit in Yerevan recognised that the world is set to miss its 2030 conservation goals, and agreed a new action plan to rescue them, without the money. Lead with the sum promised against the sum needed, in figures as the source gives them. Who holds the purse and who holds the forests: rich donors and the Global South countries the Kunming-Montreal targets depend on, as far as the source says. A plan is not a result, so say what binds anyone to it. Filed under politics because it is a negotiation, not a finding. Dateline Yerevan.

stories.label: Britain was prepared to use cluster bombs in Sierra Leone
stories.summary: Declassified files show that the UK Ministry of Defence said cluster bombs 'should be used if deemed necessary' during its 2000 intervention in Sierra Leone's civil war. Lead with that line, who signed it and what limits it set, quoted from the files. Say whether any were dropped: being prepared to use them is not using them, so do not let the reader assume it. The stake is what the intervention, sold as a humanitarian rescue, was ready to do to civilians, and Britain's later stance on the weapon, as far as the source says. Declassified UK is opinion-forward, but this rests on documents, so report the files and attribute its framing. Dateline Freetown.

stories.label: Mercado bitcoin hit by $40 million hack across 10 blockchains
stories.summary: Brazil's Mercado Bitcoin suspended deposits and withdrawals on Monday after wallets tied to it were drained of about $40 million across 10 blockchains, and it says it will absorb the loss. Lead with the frozen customers and the sum. The mechanism: how a single compromise reaches 10 chains, as far as the sources say. No one has been blamed and no public evidence ties it to the Binance hack, so say so and do not imply a link beyond the timing, days after that theft. The promise to absorb the loss is the company's own, so say when withdrawals return and who has checked. Name bitcoin. Dateline São Paulo.

stories.label: Meta Readies Cross-Border Investment Bond Offering
stories.summary: On one day the AI buildout showed both its money and its nerves: Meta is readying a cross-border investment-grade bond sale to test investors growing sceptical of the spending, and Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum for $115 billion, among the largest deals in tech history. Lead with the debt: the question is who holds the risk if the spending does not pay, as far as the sources say. These are two separate events that the feed clustered together, so say that and do not imply any link between the companies. Write the bond from Bloomberg and the deal from TechCrunch. Filed under economy; the feed's science tag is wrong. US pick 1 of 3. Dateline New York.

stories.label: Lysosomes, the cell's 'recycling centers,' found to help control heart rhythm
stories.summary: Researchers at the universities of Liverpool and Oxford found that lysosomes, known as the cell's recycling centres, also act as signalling centres in heart cells, helping the natural pacemaker respond when the heart must beat faster. Lead with that overturned job description. The mechanism: what signal they send and how it was shown, in which cells or animals, as far as the source says. Name the journal and the authors. Any use against arrhythmia is a hope and not a result, so say how far off it is. Dateline Liverpool.

stories.label: China releases timeline for lunar landing on the Moon, targeting "before 2030"
stories.summary: At the Seventh Manned Spaceflight Conference in Beijing, officials including Wang Xiang gave a timeline for landing Chinese astronauts on the Moon within three years, with no mission like Apollo 8 or Artemis II first. Lead with that skipped step and the sequence that replaces it: the Long March 10 and the lander tests still to fly, as far as the source says. What it risks and what it saves against NASA's Artemis schedule, covered in October. Keep dates as stated targets. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: Inside the Secretive, Contradictory World of Campaign Ads Funded by AI Super PACs
stories.summary: On the eve of the midterms, Bellingcat traces campaign ads funded by AI super PACs, and finds them telling contradictory stories: a Utah Democrat praised for having fought back against MAGA, and in Texas an ad promoting a Republican. Lead with that contradiction, and with what the ads leave out: whether they mention AI regulation at all. The mechanism: an industry backing candidates who may write its rules, through messages voters may not trace to it, as far as Bellingcat shows. Name the PACs, their funders and the sums, and how the ads were found. Not the horse race. US pick 2 of 3. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: 116亿元国产算力大单！大华股份拿下26.3亿
stories.summary: China Mobile's order of about 11.6 billion yuan for 20,480 AI supernode cards, all from domestic compute makers, gave 2.63 billion yuan to a subsidiary of Dahua, the smart-IoT and security-vision company, a newcomer among four established server firms. Lead with Dahua's arrival in AI compute. The turn: China Mobile owns over 5% of Dahua, so this is a related-party deal, and delivery is due in 30 days. Put it beside China Telecom's similar order of about 11.5 billion yuan in June to show the state carriers' build-out. Do not use the source's China Mobile accounts: revenue of 25.1 billion yuan against profit of 100.3 billion cannot be right. Source is Chinese; the writer reads it. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: Belgian prime minister offers resignation amid budget deadlock
stories.summary: New since the 10:00 report that he might resign: Bart De Wever has tendered his resignation, and King Philippe deferred his decision until a new meeting on Friday. Lead with that suspended state: a government neither gone nor governing. The mechanism: which debt and spending cuts split the coalition, and who would bear them, as far as the sources say. Write from Le Monde and Anadolu; TASS is state media and is attributed if used. Firstpost's 'steps down' overstates it: the king has not accepted. Dateline Brussels.

stories.label: 2026 elections live updates as Trump to speak at D.C. Reflecting Pool, and more from the campaign trail
stories.summary: New since the attacks covered 23 and 26 October and the Stevens break covered Sunday: on the eve of the vote, Democrats are rallying around Abdul El-Sayed, whose campaign says it raised over $2.4 million on Sunday alone, while the attacks on the man who could be the first Muslim US senator have escalated. Lead with the money as the campaign's own figure and what it answers: an RNC press secretary telling the New York Post he is 'a better fit for Guantanamo Bay', and Ted Cruz saying Americans could die if he sits on the Intelligence Committee. Say that those making the charges have offered no evidence, and give Rogers's answer. Not the horse race. The CBS link is a live blog, so write from Al Jazeera's report in the sources and Middle East Eye; Responsible Statecraft (https://responsiblestatecraft.org/el-sayed-anti-muslim-attacks/) is opinion-forward and may be used only for quotes it documents, attributed. US pick 1 of 3. Dateline Detroit.

stories.label: Ukrainian human rights chief says he and Russian counterpart have agreed to present joint proposal to Melania Trump
stories.summary: New since the Oleshky truce and evacuation covered in October: Ukraine's Dmytro Lubinets says he and Russia's Yana Lantratova agreed to approach Melania Trump with a joint proposal to extend the humanitarian mission to other settlements where the situation is dire. Lead with the people still trapped and which places are meant, as far as the source says. What is striking is the channel: the two countries' rights commissioners, working through the US first lady while the fighting goes on. It is one side's account of an agreement, and a proposal only, so attribute it, say whether Moscow has confirmed it, and count civilians on both sides of the line with equal care. Dateline Kyiv unless the source places the press conference elsewhere.

stories.label: PL reúne-se esta semana para debater candidatura de Rogério Marinho a presidente do Senado
stories.summary: Bolsonaro's Liberal Party meets this week to debate running Rogério Marinho, backed by Flávio Bolsonaro, for president of Brazil's Senate against Davi Alcolumbre and Tereza Cristina. Lead with the contest and what the chair controls, as far as the source says: what reaches the floor, and whatever Pública says about the courts or the presidency. Do not supply those powers from elsewhere. It is a party meeting and not a decision, so say when the vote is and what the numbers look like, if the source gives them. Picked because the audit found no Latin America dateline. Dateline Brasília.

stories.label: Nigeria's lithium boom struggles to benefit its communities
stories.summary: Nigeria is rushing to exploit its lithium, and the communities on top of it may pay through pollution, degraded land and insecurity. Lead with one mining community and what it has received against what has left, in figures if the source has them. The mechanism: who holds the licences, who buys the ore and how little is processed in Nigeria, as far as the source says; name the companies and officials it names. Keep projected jobs and growth as projections. Filed under economy; the feed's politics tag is wrong. Dateline where the source's lead community is, Dangoma if it is the case reported, otherwise Abuja.

stories.label: Nissan India October sales drop 14 pc to 8,310 units
stories.summary: India's car market passed 500,000 units in October, with Maruti Suzuki, Hyundai and Mahindra all posting records, during a war that has pushed up fuel prices across Asia. Lead with that contrast, then the mechanism the sources give: festive demand, and rising demand for CNG, which suggests buyers are moving off petrol, only as far as the sources support it. Say who is losing, with Nissan down 14% to 8,310 units. Dispatches to dealers are not sales to customers, so say which these are. Write from MoneyControl and the ABP report; the headline's Nissan figure is the smallest part. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Wheat yield sensitivity to compound hot-dry-windy events is increasing in China - Nature Food
stories.summary: A Nature Food paper finds that China's wheat yields are growing more sensitive to days that are hot, dry and windy at once. Lead with how much more sensitive, over which period and where, and the mechanism: why the compound event does more than heat or drought alone, as far as the paper shows. The stake is the world's largest wheat grower and what its imports would do to the price others pay, only as far as the paper supports that. Name the authors. Feed text is mostly references, so write from the paper. Name wheat. Dateline Beijing, or where the lead institution is.

stories.label: Meet Neuropixels: how probes that track hundreds of brain cells at once are revolutionizing neuroscience
stories.summary: Neuropixels probes, which record hundreds of neurons at once, are now going into the brains of awake patients during routine surgery: Nature opens in a London theatre where neurosurgeon Ahmed Toma implants a shunt. Lead with that scene and what a recording from a living human brain has shown that one cell at a time could not, naming a finding. Say what limits it: consent during surgery for something else, and how brief the recording is, as far as Nature does. Filed under science; the feed's politics tag is wrong. Dateline London.

stories.label: Fresh wave of fridge cyberattacks hits European supermarkets
stories.summary: New since the French attack covered 12 and 13 October: stores across Belgium, Luxembourg and Sweden reported abrupt temperature spikes in fridges and freezers early Monday, a second wave in a few weeks. Lead with the spread. The mechanism: refrigeration controllers reachable from the internet, what they have in common and whether a shared vendor links the waves, as far as the sources say; The Record's report (https://therecord.media/cyberattack-grocery-freezers-europe) is the specialist account. It is a suspected attack until an investigator says otherwise, and no attribution is to be stated as fact. Say how much food was lost and who bears it. Filed under tech; the feed's economy tag is the second-order effect. Dateline Brussels, or Stockholm if the sources lead there.

stories.label: 美团发1.6万亿参数新模型，通用Agent测试超Opus-5，国产芯特别优化
stories.summary: Meituan, a food-delivery company, released LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter model trained on Chinese accelerators with under 80GB of memory per card. Lead with that constraint and how it was worked around: parallelism rebuilt around the supernode, with the vision encoder moved out of the training graph, for a claimed 86% single-card throughput gain over the baseline. Benchmarks are Meituan's own, some on a benchmark it built, and it trails Claude Opus 5 on Terminal Bench, so say all of that and give Zhidx's hands-on findings as its own. Do not call it the best model. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: Startups recalibrate Chinese AI for the West
stories.summary: A growing number of startups are editing Chinese open-weight models for Western businesses worried about censorship and security. Lead with what the edit actually changes in a model, and on which question a before and after differs, naming the firms and models as Rest of World does. The turn worth showing: open weights let the buyer rewrite a model's values, and swapping one alignment for another is not removing one. Ask whether a backdoor or a security flaw survives such an edit, and keep the vendors' claims as theirs. Thin entry, picked because it is unique. Dateline where the source places the lead company; a US placement would count as US pick 2 of 3.

stories.label: German ministers vow tough response to Frankfurt riots and looting
stories.summary: New since the Gen Z protests covered 31 October: Frankfurt became the flashpoint, with more than 100 of 1,300 officers injured and looting, and ministers now vow a tough response. Lead with that promise and what it concretely means, as far as the sources say. The mechanism: a youth movement over education and living costs is being answered as a public-order problem. Count injured protesters with the same care as police, and say if the sources give no figure. Dateline Frankfurt.

stories.label: Belgian Prime Minister may resign on Monday
stories.summary: Budget talks have collapsed and Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever may resign after meeting King Philippe on Monday, De Standaard reports citing a source. Lead with the collapse, and report the outcome of the meeting if the sources have it; a possible resignation is not a resignation. Name what split the coalition and who would bear the cuts or taxes at issue. Write from the Reuters report on U.S. News; Mehr is state media and is attributed if used. Dateline Brussels.

stories.label: LHC seeks report from Punjab Home Department on extended detention of Imran's sisters
stories.summary: The Lahore High Court on Monday asked Punjab's Home Department for reports on pleas against the extended detention of Imran Khan's sisters and seeking medical treatment for one of them, Noreen Niazi. Lead with the women and the plea for treatment: detention reaching the family of the PTI's founder. Say what law holds them, for how long and on what grounds, and what the court does next, as far as Dawn does. The court has ruled on nothing yet, so do not write it as a win. Filed under politics; the feed's science tag is wrong. Dateline Lahore.

stories.label: Oil Declines Ahead of Midterm Elections Despite Hormuz Attacks
stories.summary: Oil fell on Monday, by more than 3% in The National's report, after Trump signalled more time for Iran diplomacy, despite the attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. Lead with that gap: the market is pricing one man's words while ships are still being hit and the Doha talks have produced nothing. Say what importers and crews still face. Do not repeat the Netanyahu call or the IRGC mine claims beyond a clause. Write from The National; the Bloomberg link is a rolling market page. Name Brent crude and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Dateline Abu Dhabi unless the source places it elsewhere.

stories.label: Ryanair to freeze pay and cut hiring as €2bn jet fuel hit looms
stories.summary: Ryanair, Europe's biggest airline, is freezing pay, scaling back hiring and raising fares to limit a €2bn rise in next year's jet fuel costs from the Iran war. Lead with the sum and who pays it: staff and passengers. The mechanism: how its fuel hedges figure in the rise, as far as the FT says. Name jet fuel, and Brent crude only if the source does. Filed under economy; the feed's science tag is wrong. Dateline Dublin.

stories.label: China signals caution over currency surge with weaker yuan fixing
stories.summary: The People's Bank of China set a weaker daily fixing on Monday even as the offshore yuan rose to a more than four-year high. Lead with that decision and the signal: Beijing is managing the pace of appreciation against outside calls for a stronger currency. Say who is calling for it and who loses from a fast rise, as far as SCMP does. Give the fixing and market rates as the source does. Name the yuan. Filed under economy; the feed's politics tag is wrong. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: China's Social Security System Fails to Narrow Inequality, Chinese Scholars Argue
stories.summary: Chinese scholars, writing in a CPC Central Party School journal, argue that China's social security system fails to narrow inequality, and call for higher farmers' pensions, lower pensions for civil servants and public-institution staff, and unified medical insurance. Lead with the gap between a farmer's pension and a civil servant's, in yuan if the source gives it. The news is where it appears: a critique of state employees' privileges inside a Party school's journal. It is a paper and not policy, so do not imply Beijing has adopted it. Name the authors and the journal, and attribute the argument to them. Filed under economy; the feed's politics tag is wrong. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: Women travel thousands of miles for a reproductive moonshot. Scientists say they've been misled
stories.summary: A STAT investigation from Tirana into three-parent IVF, mitochondrial replacement therapy, as fertility tourism: shoddy record keeping by a clinic providing the procedure, incomplete data published in marginal journals, and one puzzling ancestry test that questions the source of a child's DNA. Lead with that test. The mechanism: a technique sold across borders to women far from home, and scientists who say those women have been misled, as far as STAT shows. Give the clinic's answer, and keep the claims as STAT's findings. Dateline Tirana, so it does not count against the US cap.

stories.label: Laden with eggs, robots race up sacred Chinese mountain
stories.summary: Dozens of robots took on more than 3,000 steps of Mount Tai on Monday carrying eggs and watermelons, in a race organisers billed as a test of real-world machine endurance. Lead with what the machines actually managed: how many finished, how many failed and how fast. The mechanism: what stairs and fragile loads test that a demo floor does not, as far as the source says. Organisers' billing and state media's footage are not results, so attribute them. Mention people who carry loads up the mountain only if the source does. Dateline Tai'an.

stories.label: US has to 'take care' of one or two Iran targets - Trump
stories.summary: New beyond the Doha talks covered 1 November: Axios's sources say Netanyahu pressed Trump in a call to strike Iran immediately after Tuesday's midterms, while Trump for now wants negotiations to play out; the Israeli source called the call 'tough'. Lead with that split and its date, then Trump's own words that the US must 'take care' of one or two targets and could strike remaining nuclear sites in 10 minutes. Keep the call as anonymous sources' account. Those who would bear a resumed war are Iranians and the Gulf's crews and residents. Use Anadolu as the regional voice. Do not repeat the Doha talks beyond a clause. US pick 1 of 3. Dateline Washington unless the source places it elsewhere.

stories.label: France opens 'attempted murder' probe into petrol bomb attacks on police
stories.summary: New since the third weekend's 500 arrests covered 1 November: prosecutors opened an attempted-murder investigation after petrol bombs were thrown at security forces in Paris on Saturday, with no arrests yet for them. Lead with the charge and what it signals: the state's answer to a cost-of-living revolt is hardening. Report injuries and the video as far as the source does, and give protesters' and police's use of force equal care. Say whether a fourth weekend is planned. Dateline Paris.

stories.label: As Mahadev syndicate kingpin returns to India, a look back at the ₹6,000-crore betting racket
stories.summary: Indian agencies secured Sourabh Chandrakar's return from Oman on Sunday in the ₹6,000-crore Mahadev betting app case. Lead with the return and the sum. The mechanism: how an app run from the Gulf moved money through India, and which officials the case has reached, as far as the source says. He is accused, not convicted, so keep the allegations as the CBI's and Enforcement Directorate's, and say what happens to him next. Dateline Raipur unless the source places it elsewhere.

stories.label: NASS Roundup: Tinubu's fresh loan request, transfer of convicted Nigerians abroad, Abuja tenancy rules, other top stories from Senate
stories.summary: President Tinubu has asked the Senate to approve external loans of $20.5 billion and €1.04 billion under a 2026-2027 borrowing plan. Lead with the sum and only that item of the roundup. Who pays: Nigerians, through debt service, as far as the source gives figures, and what the money is for. Say where the request stands: it reached the Senate last Tuesday, and approval is not reported. Note the feed text gives both €1.05bn and €1.04bn, so use the figure the body supports. Dateline Abuja.

stories.label: Agriculture: How flawed wheat policy fuelled flour crisis
stories.summary: Wheat flour in Pakistan has become a daily struggle for millions of working people, and Dawn traces it to policy failure. Lead with the price of flour against a worker's wage, then the mechanism: which procurement decisions fractured the wheat and flour supply chain, and who made them, in Punjab above all. Name who profited if the source does. Keep Dawn's judgments attributed. Name wheat, so the price series can be attached. Dateline Lahore unless the source places it elsewhere.

stories.label: Binance users withdraw over $3 bln following hacker attack on crypto exchange
stories.summary: New since the FBI attribution covered 1 November: Binance reopened withdrawals, and processed $4.649 billion out against $1.01 billion in, a net outflow of about $3.64 billion. Lead with that number, the first measure of what customers did when they could leave. CoinDesk, added as the independent source, reports that Binance says it replaced about 95% of the stolen assets with company funds and will absorb the losses. Keep those as the company's claims, unaudited until its proof of reserves, promised for 3 November. Name bitcoin. Dateline: no place given by the feed's Pyongyang tag fits; use Binance's stated location only if the source gives one.

stories.label: Ukraine blames Russia after air alert app sends out false warnings
stories.summary: A civilian safety system became a weapon: Ukraine's air alert app sent false radiation warnings, and Russia said hours later that its own emergency warnings app suffered a 'massive cyberattack', as a rare humanitarian truce expired. Lead with the false radiation alert. The mechanism: what happens when people stop trusting the app that tells them to take shelter, and how the attackers got in, as far as the sources say. Each side's attribution is its own claim. TRT World is state media, so write from Al Jazeera and Deutsche Welle and attribute TRT if used. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: BTCPay tells users to turn off their servers after reports of drained wallets
stories.summary: BTCPay Server, the free open-source tool businesses use to accept bitcoin, told users on Sunday to switch off their servers after reports that attackers were draining hot wallets. Lead with the instruction: self-hosting has no central party to freeze anything, so the only defence offered is to shut down. Say what is known of the flaw, how many were hit and how much was taken, and say plainly what is not yet known. Not the Binance hack, which runs separately. No dateline place unless the source gives one.

stories.label: SenseTime open-sources 9-billion-parameter AI model that reuses layers for deeper processing
stories.summary: SenseTime released SenseNova Loop-9B-Preview, an open-source multimodal model that runs a shared block repeatedly, extending its processing depth without duplicating weights. Lead with the mechanism: depth that does not add parameters, and what that saves in memory for a Chinese lab short of advanced chips, only as far as the source supports that. Give the benchmarks as the company's own, and say what independent testing exists. Dateline Shanghai unless the source places it elsewhere.

stories.label: Crew from NASA's simulated Mars mission emerges after 378 days in isolation
stories.summary: Four volunteers left NASA's CHAPEA habitat at Johnson Space Center on Saturday after 378 days in a simulated Mars mission. Lead with what the experiment set out to measure: how crew health and performance hold under isolation, delay and scarce resources, and what data it produced. Say that results are not yet published if the source gives none, and do not present the exit itself as a finding. US pick 3 of 3. Dateline Houston.

stories.label: Cancer, Water, and Big Ag: What Rural America Is Voting On
stories.summary: Two days before the midterms, Drop Site reports what rural America is voting on: cancer, water and the power of agribusiness. Lead with one place and its numbers, and who is running against whom over it. The mechanism: an industry's hold on the land and water people live on, and whether an election can change that, as far as the source shows. Attribute health links as the source does and do not state causation it does not show. Not the horse race, and not the polling stories already run. Name no race the source does not. US pick 2 of 3. Dateline where the source's lead case is.

stories.label: Bulgaria's acting President Iotova leads in run-off exit polls
stories.summary: New since the first round covered 25 October: exit polls have Iliana Iotova ahead in Sunday's presidential run-off, on 51% in the polls cited by Bulgarian National Television. Lead with the result as exit polls, not a declared win, and with the margin. The stake: what a Bulgarian president can do on Russia, Ukraine and the Black Sea, where ships have been hit off its coast, as far as the sources say. Use Bloomberg, Al Jazeera and SCMP for the facts; TASS is state media and is attributed if used. Dateline Sofia.

stories.label: Court Dismisses Trump's Lawsuit Over the Election in Alaska
stories.summary: New since the DOJ suit covered 23 and 30 October: a federal judge dismissed the Justice Department's lawsuit that sought to halt certification of Mary Peltola if she wins, and Senator Dan Sullivan vows to honour the outcome. Lead with the ruling and its grounds, then the question it answers: whether the federal government can stop a state certifying a result before the vote. Keep the second Dan Sullivan on the ballot to a clause. The Fox link is a video; write from Al Jazeera (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1/sullivan-vows-to-honour-alaska-race-outcome-us-judge-dismisses-doj-lawsuit) and Bluewin. TRT World is state media and is attributed if used. US pick 1 of 3. Dateline Anchorage.

stories.label: More than half of Haley Stevens' staff quit over Rogers endorsement
stories.summary: New since the endorsement covered at 18:00: well over half of Stevens's congressional staff quit on Sunday in protest, and a former aide who spoke anonymously calls it a mass resignation. Lead with the walkout and the count, keep it the anonymous aide's account unless her office confirms it, and say what Stevens has answered. Why it matters: a vote two days away, and what the break says about the Democrats' split over El-Sayed; use Al Jazeera's explainer for why she did it. Do not repeat the endorsement beyond a clause, and leave the Rogers campaign's Israel registrations to the separate entry. US pick 2 of 3. Dateline Detroit unless the source places it elsewhere.

stories.label: Mike Rogers Campaign Spokesperson Is a Registered Agent for Israel, Documents Show
stories.summary: Abigail Ronson and Jesse Stokes have worked for the government of Israel, since May and last October respectively, while also working on Mike Rogers's Senate campaign, Drop Site reports from documents. Lead with the filings: what they show each was paid to do, by whom, and whether the campaign disclosed it. The accountability question: a registered foreign agent speaking for a Senate candidate two days before the vote; raise Israel's place in the race only as the source does. Say what the documents do not show, and give Rogers's answer if the source has one. US pick 3 of 3. Dateline Washington, or Detroit if the source places it there.

stories.label: MPs to vote for NPT pullout unanimously if Leader agrees
stories.summary: Former foreign minister and lawmaker Manouchehr Mottaki told national TV on Sunday that Iran's parliament would vote unanimously on leaving the Non-Proliferation Treaty if the Supreme Leader agrees. Lead with where that puts the decision: with Khamenei, not the chamber, one month after the foreign ministry confirmed withdrawal discussions on 4 October. One lawmaker's statement is not a bill, so say that. The stake: what leaving would end, inspections above all, while Iranian negotiators sit in Doha. Do not repeat the Doha talks beyond a clause. Mehr is the only source and is state media, so write that Iranian state news agency Mehr reported it, and state nothing as fact. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: Iranian ship captain martyred in US attack on vessel in PG
stories.summary: Nasser Ebrahimi Nejadian, a ship captain from Abadan, was killed by shrapnel on Friday in a US attack on a vessel in international waters of the Persian Gulf, Mehr reports. Lead with him: a named man on a working vessel, and what the ship was and who else was aboard, as far as the source says. The wider point is that the blockade's dead are mostly unnamed crews. Mehr is the only source and is state media, so write that Iranian state news agency Mehr reported it, write 'killed' rather than 'martyred', state nothing as fact, and say that no US account is in the report if there is none. Not the tanker-mine claims in the separate entry. Dateline Abadan.

stories.label: Russia suffers record 54,400 casualties in October, Ukraine says -- and 2.1M since war began
stories.summary: Ukraine counts 54,400 Russian troops killed, wounded or missing in October, its highest monthly figure of the war, about 8,170 above the month before, with Moscow losing ground to Kyiv's counterattacks. Lead with the number and whose number it is: one belligerent's count of the other, unverified, so attribute it in every use and say what it lumps together. Say what the ground changed, and give any Russian figure or independent estimate the source has. These are conscripts and contract men, many from poor regions, only if the source says so. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: Victims' families place key hidden evidence before Khampepe inquiry
stories.summary: A physical inspection of old lever arch files by lawyers for families of apartheid's victims strengthens the former prosecutor Anton Ackermann's claim that a disputed 2006 memo was forged. Lead with the file and what was found in it. The mechanism: why apartheid-era prosecutions were delayed for two decades after the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, and who stood to benefit. Keep forgery as the claim the evidence supports and not a finding, because the commission has not ruled; say who wrote the memo and what they answer, as far as the source does. Name the families' dead if the source does. Dateline Johannesburg unless the source places the hearing elsewhere.

stories.label: Retired officials call for respecting people's wishes
stories.summary: A group of retired Pakistani civil servants, diplomats and generals warns against any constitutional amendment imposed against the people's wishes and calls for equal treatment of all provinces. Lead with who signed and what amendment they mean: a warning from inside the establishment's own retired ranks is the news. Say what the proposed amendment would change for the provinces and who is pushing it, as far as Dawn does, and do not supply it from elsewhere. Their warning is theirs and not a finding. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: Iran's IRGC Navy says two tankers 'exploded' after hitting mines in Hormuz
stories.summary: New on Sunday: the IRGC Navy says two more oil tankers exploded on mines while using an 'unauthorized route' through the Strait of Hormuz, Reuters reports citing Iranian state media. Lead with the claim and the phrase: Tehran is telling shippers that the route it has not approved is mined, while its negotiators are in Doha. Keep it the IRGC's claim, and say whether any ship owner, UKMTO or another source confirms it; earlier such claims have gone unconfirmed. Who pays: crews, and importers of Gulf oil. Do not repeat the October tally or the Al Mayeda strike beyond a clause. Name Brent crude and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: Serbia shuts down bank favoured by Russians
stories.summary: Serbia's central bank revoked the licence of Alta Bank, a lender used by Russians and under international scrutiny over suspected money laundering, which is suspected of wiring large sums out of the country after former president Aleksandar Vučić lost the election. Lead with the timing: the money that moved once power changed hands, and how much, as far as the FT says. The mechanism: what a change of government exposes, one week after the students' list won. Keep the laundering and the transfers as suspicions, say who owns the bank and what it answers, and what depositors now get. Name the euro only as the source does. Dateline Belgrade.

stories.label: The Philippines’ ‘solar surge’ leaves many Filipinos behind
stories.summary: Energy prices have pushed Filipinos to solar, but the upfront cost keeps it from the households that most need the savings. Lead with the sum: what a rooftop system costs against what a poor household earns and pays for power, in pesos, as the source gives it. The mechanism: an energy shock that the better-off can buy their way out of, leaving the grid's cost to those who cannot. Say what the government or lenders offer, as far as the source does. Filed under economy because it is about who pays, not a finding. Dateline Manila.

stories.label: How SA property prices reflect municipal service delivery
stories.summary: Three days before South Africa's local elections on 4 November, house prices broadly track municipal performance, with Cape Town leading and Buffalo City lagging, and several metros breaking the pattern. Lead with the gap between the two in rand and in audit outcomes. The mechanism: a failing municipality is paid for in the value of the one asset most families own. Name the metros that break the pattern and say why, as far as the source does, and keep correlation as correlation. Not the revolt analysis run at 18:00. Dateline Cape Town unless the source places it elsewhere.

stories.label: Climate change is killing the plants of Uluṟu‑Kata Tjuṯa: Aṉangu traditional owners are concerned
stories.summary: Climate change is killing plants at Uluṟu‑Kata Tjuṯa, and the Aṉangu traditional owners are concerned. Lead with what is dying and how it was measured: which species, over what period and how sure the researchers are of the cause. The surprise: deserts are assumed to be already adapted to heat. Say what these plants are to the Aṉangu, in their words if the source gives them. Name the researchers and any journal. Thin entry, picked because it is the one real science story in this feed that is not a Scientific Reports manuscript. Dateline Uluṟu.

stories.label: Kids' social media access: FCC to hear petition on 6th
stories.summary: Pakistan's Federal Constitutional Court, a three-judge bench, hears a public interest petition on 6 November seeking to restrict social media for children under 16, and notices have gone to the federal government. Lead with the date and the ask: a court, not parliament, may decide who gets online. The mechanism: what an age limit needs in practice, identity checks on every user, and what that means in a country that already blocks platforms, as far as the source says. FCC here is the court, not the US regulator. Dateline Lahore, where the report is filed.
